characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: rolling plane of samples ground to a thickness of 1 mm
characterization_methods.purpose: phase characterization / screening of phase constitution

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: room temperature; initial strain rate 10^-3 s^-1

characterization_methods.key_findings: Hardness nearly flat around 200 HBW from 0Al to 6Al; aging increases hardness slightly for the Al-free Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy.
No cracks, pores, or macrosegregations in the final materials.
characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: cross-sectional areas prepared in the plane perpendicular to the rolling direction
characterization_methods.purpose: microstructure investigation; check for cracks, pores, or macrosegregations

processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Melting and casting in a vacuum-induction melting furnace under 400 mbar Ar pressure. Five Cu molds were moved stepwise inside the furnace and successively filled with melt from a 4-kg ingot; after each cast the remaining melt composition was adjusted by charging Al through an air lock.
10×50×130-mm³ blocks hot rolled at 1100 °C into 2±0.1-mm-thick and ~500-mm-long sheets.
Sheets reheated to 1100 °C, water quenched, and cut perpendicular to the rolling direction into sets of nine segments of 2×60×55 mm³ per alloy composition.
Homogenization at 1100 °C for 2 h under Ar, followed by water quenching. This is the parent process of the 550 °C/1 h aging step.
Aging conducted in air at 550 °C for 1 h, followed by oil quenching (one of the nine RAP heat treatments at 450/500/550/600 °C for 0/1/24 h).
Scales removed from the surfaces by low-pressure, fine-grit sandblasting after the heat treatments.
Samples for mechanical testing and microstructure investigation were prepared from the segments by package spark erosion.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Tensile specimens prepared by package spark erosion from 2×60×55 mm³ segments; all plotted values represent averages of three measurements per material state.

unmapped_findings: For the Fe-30Mn-1.2C (0 Al) reference alloy, aging leaves the yield strength virtually unchanged and increases the hardness slightly, but reduces UTS and total elongation; embrittlement becomes most apparent for long aging times (24 h) and higher temperatures (>500 °C). This qualitative trend applies to the 550 °C/1 h aged condition, but no specific numeric YS/UTS/TE values are reported for that condition in the text.

The best mechanical behavior for the Al-free ternary Fe-30Mn-1.2C alloy was reported for the as-homogenized state (360 MPa YS, 830 MPa UTS, 77% TE); these values belong to the as-homogenized sample and not to the aged-550°C-1h sample.
The as-cast samples had a coarse dendritic microstructure before hot rolling (pre-hot-rolling initial state).

The RAP screening produced a matrix of 45 different sample conditions (5 Al levels × 9 heat treatments) for the Fe-30Mn-1.2C base composition; the 550 °C/1 h condition is one of these nine heat treatments.
